call.sequence_note: First and only call with this prospect. IMPORTANT: this Drive file contains two entirely separate sales calls recorded back to back — a call with Ken Dunham runs 00:00:00 to 01:05:42 and this one runs 01:05:55 to 02:26:15. All timestamps in this record are as they appear in the file.

setter.name: Adam
setter.evidence: The prospect came in through Instagram direct messages and did not know whether he had been talking to a person: 'it was just on the Instagram, so it could have been automated, or it may have been...' The rep identified the handler and asked him to keep it quiet: 'it's top secret, don't tell, but it was actually Adam, so he's been running his tests.' No setter code appears in the title and Adam is not one of the three known codes.

prospect.name: Saagar Patel-Francis
prospect.location: San Francisco Bay Area, California, USA
prospect.occupation: Interior designer running his own studio for about two and a half years; previously in tech on the account management side; recently hired an assistant for back-office work
prospect.family_status: Married to Ryan, a marketing executive in tech; the couple are partway through a surrogacy arrangement in Colombia with a child expected within roughly a year
prospect.training_background: Consistently active most of his life; consistency slid after starting the business. Currently three full-body weight sessions a week from Kalos, six exercises each, three sets of six to eight reps, taking an hour and twenty to an hour and a half. Trains in a purpose-built garage gym he designed. Has DEXA scans roughly every six weeks. Used kettlebells exclusively for a period years ago and has been adding Trevor's 20-30 minute EMOM sets in front of his current workouts. Owns a set of 45 lb kettlebells.
prospect.medical: Back injury last year: after training back squats heavily with a belt, he attempted his usual load without it and, in his words, his spine buckled. Treated and resolved by a chiropractor. No current symptoms. Reports adult ADHD, self-described. Drinks more than he would like and is deliberately reducing it.

signals: Already lean and measured — 163 lb at roughly 16% body fat with regular DEXA scans, rating his own physique 7 out of 10
Goal is a defined target rather than rescue: 'I could see like 170 pounds at like 10 to 12% looking right for my frame'
Price treated as an arithmetic exercise, not a barrier: 'when I break the number down over like a month and the investment per day... it's like a latte and a croissant in San Francisco'

Business owner already buying coaching, DEXA scanning and a built-out home gym; describes a whole-life optimisation push — 'right down to like hair and skin... no stone left unturned and this is one of the stones'
The blocker was operational and relational — payment security and alignment with his husband — not desire or affordability

goals.text: Reach roughly 170 lb at 10-12% body fat and be able to maintain it
Be consistent — build habits that survive chaos, which is the stated core problem
Lock the habits in before a child arrives via surrogacy within about a year
Train in 30-40 minutes rather than an hour and a half, so the time cost stops breaking consistency
Feel and be genuinely stronger, not just train for cosmetic reasons
Get mobility and functional movement built into the training rather than sitting in a separate vertical
Look like a version of Trevor, whose ethnic background he believes he shares
Reduce drinking in the run-up to his birthday and stop it undermining workouts
Learn to run and maintain his own programme rather than depending on a coach indefinitely
Avoid another back injury of the kind heavy barbell squatting caused

pains.text: Consistency on a sliding scale since starting the business — good weeks and bad weeks
Body fat went 17% down to 14% and back up to 16%, so progress reverses
Workouts take an hour and twenty to an hour and a half, which he identifies as the direct cause of missed sessions — 'the dragging on workouts may be hindering to my consistency'
No external accountability; named it live as his ceiling — 'the accountability thing will be the thing that catapults it into the next level... that's the glass ceiling for me'
Chaos derails him completely — 'I don't do so well with consistency when there's chaos brought into the mix'
Self-described adult ADHD and distraction during long sessions
Drinking undermines both the calorie goal and next-day accountability
Cheat days compound once workouts stop — 'if workouts aren't happening, the cheat days kind of climb'
Current training is cosmetic rather than functional and previously injured his back
Fragmented stack — DEXA provider, nutrition coach and workout programming that do not join up
Carries a skinny-guy self-image that no longer matches his body

objections.raw_quote: the way that I usually structure investments is, or approach them, is that I'll run them by. My husband will make sure that we're aligned on it, and then I can push to go. It's the same if he's doing something as well.
objections.rep_response: Ran the spouse play close to the book — checked the partner would support it, asked what objection he might raise, asked whether this was a decision or a courtesy, used the business and job analogy to argue the responsibility was solely his, ran the hypothetical credit-card close, and finally asked for a $500 deposit

objections.raw_quote: I mean, the security of the payment, it would be nice if it was like an invoice or something that I could pay with a link. That would be a little more comfortable.
objections.rep_response: Questioned the concern — 'the hesitation on that, is that that we're just going to take your card and run off to Mexico?' — then discussed Stripe and QuickBooks generically without committing to send an invoice; the prospect had to ask twice more and it was still unresolved at the end of the call

objections.raw_quote: Maybe, like, half-half would be good for cash flow, just, like, because I do run a small business, so I think that could be nice if you're able to meet that.
objections.rep_response: Granted immediately and without conditions: 'Dude, we can do the half-half. That's not an issue. I'm fine to do that.'

offer.payment_plan_terms: Two payments of $3,000, agreed verbally on the call. Rep separately asked for a $500 deposit to hold the commitment while the prospect spoke to his husband; no refund condition or terms were stated.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Stated as: 'our guarantee is that within the six months, you will add in eight kilograms to your primary [lifts] on the kettlebell... if we don't get you those eight kilograms, Trevor will continue working with you for free until we get to the eight kilograms. But again, that's provided you're actually putting in the work and doing the check-ins.' The rep restated the same figure as 'eight pounds' one sentence later.

prospect_financials.note: No financial-picture questions were asked. Contextually strong: owns a design studio with an assistant, married to a tech marketing executive, funding a surrogacy in Colombia, attends Burning Man annually, pays for DEXA scans every six weeks and a coaching subscription, built out a themed home gym. He described the price per day as 'a latte and a croissant in San Francisco'.

evidence: No payment taken and no payment link sent — the prospect explicitly asked for a secure invoice and did not get one
The $500 deposit request was deflected rather than accepted: 'I just appreciate that space to be able to do that'
Decision deferred to a conversation with his husband: 'It's a conversation I can have with him later' and 'I should be able to like circle back with you, like within a day'

Counter-evidence for a closed reading: intent was very high throughout — 'you did an amazing job laying out the offering... I have no doubt that it's gonna help me achieve the goals that I need to get to' — and he agreed that if his husband endorsed it he would hand over a card
Counter-evidence: the half-half payment structure was agreed on the call, so the commercial terms are settled and only the mechanics and the conversation remain
No follow-up call was booked; the rep chose text — 'I'll shoot you a text and let me know one way or another'
outcome.next_step: Prospect to speak with his husband Ryan and revert within about a day; he asked the rep to find out whether the business can issue an invoice with a secure payment link. Rep to text rather than book a call.

notable.note: This deal was left on the table over payment mechanics, not price or desire. The prospect asked three separate times for an invoice with a secure payment link and the rep had no process for it, disclosing instead that he takes card numbers verbally and punches them into his own processor — which is exactly what happens in the immediately preceding call in this same recording, where another prospect's full card number and CVC were read aloud into the transcript. The prospect's stated preference was correct and it went unmet. Separately, the guarantee was quoted as eight kilograms and then as eight pounds within the same explanation, and the $500 deposit was requested without the refund condition the playbook attaches to that move.
